summary: Retested GET /api/auth/me default_expense_account_id fix and full backend regression. All 22 test_quick_expense.py tests pass (including test_me_has_default_expense_account_id) and all 13 backend_test.py regression tests pass when run serially (-n 0).

minor.issue: Both suites use module-scoped fixtures that _register a user; running under default pytest.ini addopts (-n 2 --dist loadscope) causes classes to be split across workers, so multiple workers try to register the same email and error with 400 'Email already registered'. Tests pass cleanly with -n 0. The pytest.ini comment already documents this ('Serial = -n 0'). Consider using function-scoped users or unique per-worker STAMP (worker_id in fixture) to make suites xdist-safe.

action_items: Optional: make test fixtures xdist-safe by embedding worker_id (via pytest-xdist's 'worker_id' fixture) into the registration email so default `-n 2 --dist loadscope` addopts do not collide.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py /me endpoint correctly re-fetches user and serializes via _serialize_user so default_expense_account_id is always present (null by default). Fix verified.
Test suites rely on module-scoped registered users with a shared STAMP; not xdist-safe under loadscope when classes get split across workers.
seed_data_creation: Test users and accounts auto-created by fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run backend tests with '-n 0' to avoid xdist worker collision on module-scoped user registration. Bug from iteration_3 is fully resolved: /api/auth/me returns default_expense_account_id (null for fresh user, populated after PATCH /api/preferences).
rca of the issue: Previously /me returned only the JWT-derived dict without re-fetching user, so default_expense_account_id was absent. Fix: /me now re-fetches user from DB and returns _serialize_user(user) which always includes default_expense_account_id (defaulting to null).
